transcript: Doctor: Hi Mr. Torres, welcome back for your annual wellness visit. How have things been going? Patient: Pretty good overall. I've been trying to exercise more like we talked about last year. Walking about thirty minutes most days. Doctor: That's fantastic, keep that up. Any new concerns since your last visit? Patient: Well my knees have been bothering me a bit when I go up stairs. And I've been waking up to use the bathroom two or three times a night which is new. Doctor: When did the nighttime urination start? Patient: Maybe two or three months ago. No burning or pain, just frequency. Doctor: Okay we'll check a PSA and urinalysis today to screen for anything. You're fifty four so that's a reasonable time to start monitoring. Let me look at your vitals. Blood pressure one forty four over ninety two, that's a bit elevated from last year. Weight is two twelve, down four pounds from last visit. Patient: I was hoping the walking would help with the blood pressure too. Doctor: It does help but we may need to consider starting a low dose medication if it stays in this range. I'd like you to do some home monitoring for two weeks and log the readings. Fasting glucose was ninety eight on your labs which is borderline so we'll add a hemoglobin A1C today. Patient: My father was diabetic so I worry about that. Doctor: Your family history makes screening important. We'll also do a lipid panel. You're due for a colonoscopy referral at your age as well. Let me put that in. Patient: Sounds like a full workup. Doctor: Preventive care is the best care. We'll review everything at your follow up in three weeks.
